text:
Carter Verhaeghe went 82nd overall, bounced through the AHL and has three Stanley Cup rings. Twenty-one games into this season he has 10 goals, 10 assists and a three-assist night against Detroit, still the Panthers' most dependable scorer outside the marquee names.

His own finishing is a little hot (10 goals on 7.7 expected), but the bigger number is around him. Florida has scored 11 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice, and at five on five the team plays about as well with him as without him (52% of the expected goals either way). That kind of on-ice luck fades, so we'd expect the points to slow even if he keeps playing well.

And he does play well in the parts that don't show up on the scoresheet. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had 72% of his zone exits leaving with possession last season and put him in the 93rd percentile among forwards in setting up shots. Evolving-Hockey noted he faces top competition. He's the kind of player who makes a deep team deeper, whatever the shooting percentage does.
